prior_exposure: All original confirmation results are known. The extension responds to their strong-baseline failure: the simple linear tilt has about 74 times less observed relative variance than interval minimax on the main case. No claim that these models are a blind new benchmark. The new seeds have not been run.
construction: Propagate finite binary-flip separation envelopes using z^3/4 <= a^3-b^3 <= 3z-3z^2+z^3 on [-1,1], rather than replacing the divided difference by a derivative range. Sum impulse envelopes against the positive score. Use 80-bit dyadic outward arithmetic and recompute actual 32-bit proposal certificates.
planned_checks: Derive scalar envelopes and monotonicity exactly; independently challenge via existing native verification agent.
Check every bit flip of the same d=2,T=8 exhaustive fixture; distinguish binary64 checking from proof.
Check finite-difference lower >= original derivative lower and upper <= original derivative upper up to outward-grid rounding.
Compare exact minimax certificates and width budgets on all three already exposed cases.
Run the new midpoint probability and midpoint log-odds proposals on the main case, using a path count chosen solely from the new certificate; compare with the unchanged original linear-tilt baseline.

A materially sharper certificate means at least 20 percent fewer certified trajectories on the main case. No practical superiority claim unless cost-normalized observed variance beats the linear tilt. Any failure remains in the record.
costs: Charge acquisition, proposal certificate, numerical setup, aggregation, and simulation separately; preserve the original code and data without editing.
possible_followup: If the finite-change compiler remains pessimistic, identify a provable information obstruction or derive state/background-sensitive bounds. Do not relabel the extension as independent confirmation.
privacy: Private. No publication or extra worker allocation.
